setupSteps: Warm up first. 2 to 5 minutes of walking on the spot, arm circles, gentle hip circles and a few easy squats. Do not drop into a deep lunge with cold legs.
Floor. Flat and non-slip. A sticky mat or bare feet on a dry floor; never socks on tiles. The back foot must not slide.
Stance room. Face the long side of the room or the mat. Clear about 1.4 m by 1 m for the legs and 2 m of height for the arms (est.).

Wall or chair (optional). For the wall version, stand with your back about one foot-length from a smooth wall so the back heel can touch it. For the chair version, a sturdy chair with its back against a wall, beside the front leg.
Clothing. Stretchy pants or shorts; a long kurta tucked in so you can see the knees; no tight jeans.
Mark the stance. Step the feet apart once, check the distance (about 3.5 to 4 feet, est.), then keep the same distance for the next side.
Camera. Phone on a shelf at hip height, 2.5 to 3 m in front, so the whole body, both feet and the hands are in frame (see sections 11 and 12).

steps.title: Stand tall in Tadasana
steps.action: feet together, arms by the sides, weight even on both feet.
steps.visualCheck: front view, head over the hips, shoulders level.

steps.title: Step the feet apart
steps.action: step the left foot back about 3.5 to 4 feet (about 105 to 120 cm, est.), with the right foot forward. Hold the hands on the hips.
steps.feel: a long, steady base; the back leg stretching a little.
steps.visualCheck: front view, feet well apart, front foot pointing straight ahead.

steps.title: Set the back foot (Warrior I)
steps.action: turn the left (back) foot out about 45 degrees (sources: 45 to 60). Keep the heel down if you can; if the heel lifts, raise it a little rather than twisting the knee.
steps.feel: the outer edge of the back foot grounded; no twist in the back knee.
steps.visualCheck: front view, back foot angled out, back kneecap points along the back toes.

steps.title: Turn the hips toward the front
steps.action: turn the pelvis toward the front of the mat as far as comfortable. A perfectly square pelvis is not required; let the back hip stay slightly open if the back knee or lower back complains.
steps.feel: the back hip stretching, not the back knee.
steps.visualCheck: front view, both hip points roughly level and facing the camera.

steps.title: Bend the front knee
steps.action: bend the right knee so it moves forward over the ankle, tracking over the second toe (towards the pinky-toe side, not inward). Stop when the knee is above the ankle; never let it pass the toes. Keep the back leg straight but soft.
steps.feel: the front thigh and buttock working; the back-leg hip flexor stretching.
steps.visualCheck: front view, the knee over the middle toes, no inward collapse; you can still see your toes past the knee.

steps.title: Lift the arms (Warrior I)
steps.action: breathe in and raise both arms overhead, palms facing, shoulder-width. Shorter: hands on the hips. Gentler for shoulders: arms in a V.
steps.feel: ribs lifting; the shoulders soft, not shrugged.
steps.visualCheck: front view, wrists above the shoulders, arms straight, neck long.

steps.title: Choose the gaze
steps.action: look straight ahead, or up at the hands if the neck is comfortable.
steps.visualCheck: chin not poking forward; head over the shoulders.

steps.title: Hold Warrior I
steps.action: press both feet down, lift the chest, keep the torso upright over the pelvis (not leaning over the front leg or arching the lower back).
steps.feel: leg work, a stretch in the front of the back hip; no pinch in the lower back or knees.
steps.tempo: about 15 to 30 seconds (est.; 5 breaths is about 25 seconds).

steps.title: Open to Warrior II
steps.action: breathe out, lower the arms; turn the whole pelvis and chest to face the long side of the room, as the back foot turns to about 90 degrees (parallel to the short edge of the mat). Keep the front knee over the ankle. The front heel lines up with the back foot's arch (or a little closer if you feel unstable).
steps.feel: the inner thighs opening; the front knee steady.
steps.visualCheck: front view, hips open towards the long side of the mat, torso centred over the pelvis.

steps.title: Extend the arms (Warrior II)
steps.action: raise both arms to shoulder height, palms down, reaching in one line from fingertip to fingertip. Back wrist roughly over the back ankle.
steps.feel: wide chest; shoulders soft; arms light.
steps.visualCheck: front view, arms level and in one line, shoulders directly above the hips.

steps.title: Gaze over the front hand
steps.action: turn the head and look over the front fingertips; if the neck is tender, look straight ahead.

steps.title: Hold Warrior II
steps.action: keep pressing the feet down, the front knee tracking over the second toe, the torso upright, the arms up.
steps.feel: heat in the front thigh and shoulders; mild effort, not burning pain.
steps.visualCheck: front knee not collapsing in; shoulders not lifting to the ears.

steps.title: Come out
steps.action: straighten the front leg, lower the arms, turn the feet forward and step the back foot to the front. Rest in Tadasana for 2 to 3 breaths.
steps.visualCheck: no jerking up with the neck.

steps.title: Switch
steps.action: repeat on the other side (left foot forward). Do both sides each round.

commonMistakes.title: Front knee past the toes
commonMistakes.text: Front knee past the toes. It loads the kneecap and knee joint more. Fix: take the front foot a little farther forward, or bend less; if you cannot see your toes past the knee, back off.

commonMistakes.title: Front knee collapsing inward
commonMistakes.text: Front knee collapsing inward. It twists the knee and often means weak outer hips. Fix: press the outer edge of the front foot down and steer the knee toward the little-toe side.

commonMistakes.title: Forcing the hips square in Warrior I
commonMistakes.text: Forcing the hips square in Warrior I. Pulling the back hip forward can torque the back knee and strain the sacroiliac joint. Fix: let the back hip stay a little open; widen the stance a little; lift the back heel if the ankle is tight.

commonMistakes.title: Back foot too straight, or heel dragged down
commonMistakes.text: Back foot too straight, or heel dragged down. It twists the back knee or compresses the lower back. Fix: turn the back foot out about 45 degrees (I) or about 90 degrees (II); lift the heel a little if needed.

commonMistakes.title: Leaning forward and arching the lower back
commonMistakes.text: Leaning forward and arching the lower back. The torso falls over the front leg. Fix: lift the chest, draw the tailbone down, shorten the stance, or place hands on hips.

commonMistakes.title: Shrugged shoulders and craned neck
commonMistakes.text: Shrugged shoulders and craned neck. It strains the neck and shoulders. Fix: draw the shoulders down, lower the arms, or place hands on hips; look ahead.

commonMistakes.title: Stance too short, or too long
commonMistakes.text: Stance too short, or too long. Too short makes a deep knee bend and a tipped pelvis; too long makes it hard to hold. Fix: adjust until the front shin is vertical and you can breathe.

commonMistakes.title: Holding the breath
commonMistakes.text: Holding the breath. It raises effort and can make you dizzy. Fix: slow nose breaths; lower the arms if needed.

commonMistakes.title: Warrior II: leaning toward the front leg, or sinking the hips
commonMistakes.text: Warrior II: leaning toward the front leg, or sinking the hips. Fix: keep the torso centred over the pelvis, back wrist over the back ankle.

safetyNotes: Mild effort, never pain. Stop at pain in the knee, hip, lower back, neck or shoulder.

Knee: knee over the ankle and over the second toe; no inward collapse, no knee past the toes. One source warns that the Warriors can strain the ACL if the knee is not kept in line with the ankle. A shallower bend suits knee problems.

Hip and back: a slightly open back hip is fine in Warrior I; do not force the hips square. Warrior II is sometimes taught with strain on the hip, sacroiliac joints and lower back, so check the hips are not tilting.
Shoulder and neck: overhead arms can aggravate a rotator cuff (a source says so); use hands on hips or a V. Neck problems: look ahead, do not turn or tilt the head up.
Ankle: one health guide lists ankle injury among reasons to avoid the pose; use a chair for support or skip.
Blood pressure and dizziness: do not hold the breath; avoid keeping the arms overhead for long; come out slowly; if you feel dizzy, sit down.
Stop immediately if you feel: sharp pain in the knee, hip or back, numbness or tingling, dizziness, chest pain or breathlessness, or a pop or pull.
Spotter: not needed; use a wall or chair.
Gym etiquette: use a clear mat area and keep the chair out of the walkway.

Stance length: 3.5 to 4 feet, 4 to 4.5 feet (Iyengar), or as long as you can manage. We chose about 3.5 to 4 feet, shorter for beginners.
Front-knee depth: about 90 degrees is the classic ideal; more than 90 is fine if the knee complains. We chose knee over ankle, about 90 to 120 degrees (est.).
Back foot: about 45 degrees (Warrior I; some say 45 to 60); about 90 degrees (Warrior II; some use a looser angle).
Back heel in Warrior I: down (traditional) versus lifted (modern, more accessible but less stable). We chose heel down if comfortable, lifted a little if not.
Square hips: traditional teaching says square them; others call full squaring a myth. We chose "only as far as the knee and back allow".
Hold time: 3 to 5 breaths, 5 to 10 breaths, or 30 to 60 seconds. We chose 3 to 5 breaths.

Not found: official CYP text for Warrior I and II (and whether they are in the CYP at all); MDNIY technique page; Warrior-specific MET; measured joint-angle norms or EMG data; wall-specific front-knee cue; clinical condition sources (ACOG, AHA, ADA for this pose). Our thresholds are estimates.
